questions.question: By the de Bruijn–Klarner theorem, can a $10 \times 14$ board be tiled by $1 \times 4$ bars?

options.text: Yes, by placing bars along the boundary first
Only if two opposite corners are removed

questions.explanation: An $m \times n$ rectangle can be tiled by $1 \times k$ bars if and only if $k \mid m$ or $k \mid n$, proved via $\omega^{i+j}$ weights.

questions.question: In the proof that $R(3, 4) \le 9$, what rules out the balanced case where every vertex in $K_9$ has exactly $3$ red edges and $5$ blue edges?
questions.explanation: A $3$-regular red subgraph on $9$ vertices would require degree sum $27$, violating the handshake lemma ($2|E|$ is even).

questions.question: By Goodman's bound, what is the minimum number of monochromatic triangles in any red/blue edge coloring of $K_6$?
What is the Schur number $S(2)$, the largest $N$ admitting a $2$-coloring of $[N]$ with no monochromatic solution to $x + y = z$?
questions.explanation: Red $\{1, 4\}$ and blue $\{2, 3\}$ works on $[4]$, whereas $[5]$ forces a monochromatic sum.
